transcript.text: dehumidifer in the garage hasnt collected any water for weeks, fan is runnin. is it broke? its a meaco

Not necessarily broken. There are a few common reasons a Meaco can run its fan but collect no water, especially in a garage at this time of year.

1. It's too cold (most likely if it's a compressor model)
Compressor dehumidifiers (e.g. Meaco Arete, 12L/20L/25L compressor models) lose a lot of efficiency below about 15°C. In a cold garage they:
• Go into defrost mode frequently, where the fan runs but the compressor stops
• Pull very little water even when working
• Garages also often have low absolute moisture when cold, so there's less to collect

Desiccant models (e.g. Meaco DD8L) work much better in cold spaces. If yours is a compressor type, that's likely the issue.

2. Check the settings
• Humidity target: if it's set to, say, 60% and the garage is already below that, the compressor won't kick in and only the fan runs. Try setting it to the lowest level or "continuous."
• Mode: make sure it's not on fan-only or a laundry/air-purify mode.

3. Check where the water is going
• Is a continuous drain hose fitted? Water may be draining out instead of into the tank.
• Make sure the tank is seated properly and the float inside moves freely.

4. Quick test to see if it's actually working
Move it into a warm room in the house (around 20°C) and run it on continuous for a few hours. Then check:
• Is the air coming out noticeably warmer than the room? On a compressor model, it should be.
• Can you hear the compressor hum/vibrate, not just the fan?
• Does water appear after a few hours?

If it works indoors, it's fine; the garage is just too cold for it.
If it's still warm-room, continuous mode, compressor silent, air not warm, and no water, then it's likely a compressor or refrigerant fault. Contact Meaco: they have a good reputation for support, and many models carry a 2-year warranty or longer if registered.

If you tell me the model name/number, I can be more specific.
its the Meaco 20L low energy, about 3 yrs old. display says humidity 55% and target is set to 60% if that matters. worked great all summer, only stopped since it got cold about 4 weeks ago

Yes, that matters a lot, and it's good news. Your dehumidifier is almost certainly fine.

Why it's not collecting water
The garage is at 55% and your target is 60%, so it thinks the job's done. The compressor (the part that actually pulls water out) switches off, and the fan keeps running to sample the air so it knows when to start again. That's normal behaviour.

Why it changed when the weather turned
In summer the air holds much more moisture, so it was constantly working to get down to 60%. Now that it's colder there's less moisture to remove, and the garage is sitting below your target without much help.

If you want to confirm it still works
Set it to continuous mode (or the lowest target) and listen for the compressor kicking in: a deeper hum or slight vibration on top of the fan noise. Give it a few hours and you should see some water. It'll be slow in a cold garage, because compressor models like the 20L Low Energy lose efficiency as temperatures drop and will pause to defrost more often, but it should collect something.

Do you need to change anything?
Probably not. 55% is a good level for a garage. Keeping it below about 60% is what prevents mould, rust and damp smells, so your current setting is doing its job. You could leave it as is, or even switch it off on dry spells to save electricity.

Worth knowing for winter
If the garage gets properly cold (low single figures °C), a compressor unit will struggle. If you find humidity creeping above 60–65% in deep winter and it can't keep up, a desiccant dehumidifier would handle those temperatures much better.
